cupolaState.text:
Cupolayes
    
      
      Why Other work proposed bounded trial, implementing owner adoption in other work (2026-11-03): show the square body under its separate pyramid cap pictured on each Currey blockhouse. Occurrence on the selected 1812-08-14 prototype is an owner-adopted reconstruction, not a finding that it was built. Whistler explicitly says the cupolas were not yet built in 1808; no completion date is known, and this attribute does not claim presence throughout the parent fort's 1803-1812 range. The existing kit supplies a 1.8 m body, 2.1 m total body height, 0.22 m cap eave, 36-degree cap pitch and 0.12 m roof seat: every number is reconstructed and inherited as a trial, not measured from Currey or transferred as evidence from the second fort. No louvres, glazing, interior, function or finial is asserted. Actual native comparison must show useful improvement; other first-fort proportions and image differences remain open.

        'Bird’s-Eye View of Old Fort Dearborn.' Illustration at p. 27 of J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912). Numbered reconstruction of the first fort, not a contemporary view.
       source · archived
      Whistler, Captain John. "Fort Dearborn" [draught of the garrison and its vicinity], dated in the parade 'January 25th 1808', with its 'Index annexed to the Draught of Fort Dearborn &c.' signed at Fort Dearborn 20 February 1808. Original in the files of the War Department, Washington. Reproduced as the plate 'Fort Dearborn and Vicinity in 1808. From the original draft by Captain Whistler in the archives of the War Department at Washington', facing p. 164 of Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835 (Chicago, 1913); the index is printed in full in note 413 on the same pages.
       source · archived
